analysis:
Reviewed the two base_text excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md (base lines 4495-5336) plus the file_changes patch excerpt. The change is documentation only: it updates the 'Last updated' date, adds Gemma 4 serial-prefill pipeline default-width notes (head ~126-129, 3048-3049, 3100-3101), and rewrites some sections (head 4505-4538 manifest-pin/qualification alias text, 4901-4927 Qwen27 vision residency and media transport wording). No code, wire protocol, key handling, attestation, prefix-cache storage or authorization behavior changes in the supplied evidence, so I found no new attack surface or regression against the TB-002/TB-007/TB-011 threat entries or T-041.

The base text shows qualification and serving-grant scoping by runtime identity and artifact (DistributedInstalledPairServingGrant). The head side documents that the two Gemma 26B aliases are accepted only for an exact registered aggregate and that a run of one alias supplies no grant for the other. This is consistent with existing grant scoping.

Open integration questions: the patch excerpt is truncated, so the underlying source change that makes serial-prefill Gemma 4 pipelines default to a width greater than one is not visible. That was not verifiable here. If the PR also changes the installed lane default in code, the next pass should check that per-request admission and LOAD memory gates, owner-lease width agreement, and pair-serving grant gating still apply at the new default, and that the multi-lane prefix-cache scope (tenant partitions, T-041) is unaffected. The head text for these changes is not in the supplied units, so I cannot assess it. Documentation drift alone is not a finding.
